transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I keep rechecking and fixing how I look before I go out or get on camera, and it’s starting to make me late and stressed all the time. It's gotten really exhausting, so my sister encouraged me to come in and get some help.
Can you tell me more about what you're checking or fixing when you're getting ready, is it specifically related to your appearance or are there other things you're checking as well?

Yes, it is specifically about my appearance—I get hyper-focused on my face, worrying that my jaw looks crooked and my skin looks bad. I get stuck in front of the mirror adjusting my hair, changing shirts repeatedly, and taking multiple test selfies just to try and look "less ugly" before anyone sees me.
Do you ever experience intrusive thoughts or images that are not related to your appearance, or is your distress primarily focused on how you look?

No, I don't really have any other intrusive thoughts or worries like that. My distress is almost entirely focused on my appearance, especially things like my jaw, skin, and hair. All of my anxiety and overthinking always seem to tie back to how I look to other people.

Can you tell me if you also have repetitive behaviors or mental acts that you feel driven to perform in response to your concerns about your appearance, or is it mainly the preoccupation with how you look that's causing you distress?

It is definitely both the constant worrying and the repetitive behaviors that I feel a strong drive to do. I get stuck in front of the mirror adjusting my hair, changing shirts, and taking test selfies over and over to feel "less ugly" before going out or getting on video calls. Doing all of that easily wastes 20 to 30 minutes every time, which is why I'm always running late.

Can you describe how you would feel or what would happen if you were prevented from performing these repetitive behaviors, such as being unable to check your appearance in a mirror or take test selfies before going out?

To be honest, I haven't actually tried to stop myself from doing these routines, so I'm not completely sure. But I think I would feel extremely anxious and self-conscious, absolutely terrified of people seeing me looking ugly or imperfect.

Have you ever felt the need to perform these repetitive behaviors, such as checking or adjusting your appearance, in response to a specific thought or image that isn't related to your appearance, or are they always directly about how you look?

No, they are always directly about how I look. I only feel driven to do these things because of thoughts about my crooked jaw, bad skin, or just wanting to feel "less ugly" before going out or getting on camera. It's never triggered by any unrelated thoughts or urges.

Have you ever experienced any significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life due to your obsessive thoughts or compulsive behaviors related to your appearance, and if so, can you give me an example?

Yes, it has definitely caused problems in my life. I’ve been running late to my CNC shifts and my volunteer STEM sessions because I get stuck getting ready, which actually led to my supervisor commenting on my punctuality. I've also started skipping group photos and hanging out less, and my friends are starting to say I'm pulling away.

Can you clarify if your repetitive behaviors, such as checking and adjusting your appearance, are aimed at preventing a specific feared outcome or consequence, such as being ridiculed or rejected by others, rather than just trying to feel less ugly or more comfortable with how you look?

While my immediate urge in front of the mirror is just to feel "less ugly" and more comfortable, a huge part of it is definitely the fear of being judged or teased. Some teasing comments from my teammates and relatives about how I looked in a photo really stuck with me, and I'm terrified of being laughed at or rejected again.

You've mentioned that your behaviors are focused on your appearance, but can you tell me if you've ever had any compulsions or urges to repeat behaviors that aren't related to how you look, such as checking locks or counting, even if they're not as frequent or distressing as your appearance concerns?
No, I don't have any urges to do things like check locks or count. All of my repetitive habits and anxieties are strictly focused on my appearance and how I look.

You've mentioned that your distress and behaviors are entirely focused on your appearance, but I want to clarify one more time: are you absolutely certain you've never experienced any repetitive behaviors or urges that aren't related to how you look, no matter how small or insignificant they might seem?
Yes, I'm absolutely sure. I really can't think of any repetitive behaviors or urges that are unrelated to my appearance. My habits and anxiety are entirely focused on how I look.
